component.name: stream
component.title: Stream
component.description: Read from System.in, a file or an HTTP URL, and write to System.out, System.err, a file or an output stream in a message header.
component.label: file,core

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelStreamIndex.label: consumer
CamelStreamIndex.description: The index of the exchange in the stream, starting at 0 and counting each exchange that the consumer creates: a line, a group of lines, or the bytes of one read. With scanStream and retry, the count goes on after the stream is opened again.

CamelStreamComplete.label: consumer
CamelStreamComplete.description: Whether the exchange is the last one of the stream. The consumer reads one line ahead to know it, except for kind in, where it is true for each line. Always false with scanStream, as a scanned stream never ends.

consumerOut.description: Each line of the stream as text. With groupLines, a List of the lines; with readLine=false, all the bytes of the stream (with scanStream, the bytes read in one scan)

producerIn.description: Text in the encoding, or bytes, a stream or a file as bytes, followed by a new line; no body writes nothing. A Map or a POJO is written as its toString() and a List fails: marshal it first

kind.description: The kind of stream. The consumer reads from in (System.in), file (the file of fileName) or http (the URL of httpUrl). The producer writes to out (System.out), err (System.err), file (the file of fileName) or header (the java.io.OutputStream in the stream header of the message). Any other kind fails when the consumer or producer is created.

encoding.description: The name of the charset of text, for example UTF-8. The consumer uses it to read lines with kind in or file, reads lines of kind http with the JVM default charset, and does not use it with readLine=false. The producer uses it to write a body that is a String or that cannot be converted to byte[]. If not set, the JVM default charset is used.

fileName.description: The path of the file that kind file reads or writes. The consumer reads the file from the beginning; without scanStream, a file that cannot be read fails the start of the consumer. The producer appends to the file, and creates it and its parent directories when they do not exist.

fileWatcher.label: consumer
fileWatcher.description: Whether the consumer watches the directory of fileName with the JDK WatchService for the creation or modification of the file, for example when it is overwritten or rolled over. Only for kind file, and only used with scanStream and retry: the consumer then opens the file again at its end only when it changed. A fileName without a directory is not watched.

groupLines.label: consumer
groupLines.description: The number of lines that the consumer puts in one exchange, whose body is the result of groupStrategy, by default a List of the lines. If 0, each line is one exchange. Without scanStream, the lines left at the end of the stream are sent as a smaller group, and with scanStream a group is sent only when it is full. With kind in and without scanStream, each line is sent alone. Not used with readLine=false.

groupStrategy.label: consumer
groupStrategy.description: The org.apache.camel.component.stream.GroupStrategy that turns a group of lines into the message body. Only used when groupLines is set. The default returns the List of the lines as is.

httpHeaders.label: consumer
httpHeaders.description: The request headers that the consumer sends to httpUrl, as a comma-separated list of name=value or name:value pairs, for example Accept:application/json. Whitespace around each name and value is removed. A value that contains a comma, = or : is not supported.

httpUrl.label: consumer
httpUrl.description: The URL that kind http reads from, which the consumer opens with java.net.URLConnection. Without scanStream, the consumer opens it when it starts, so a URL that cannot be reached fails the start.

initialPromptDelay.label: consumer
initialPromptDelay.description: The delay in milliseconds before the first prompt of promptMessage, used in place of promptDelay. It keeps the prompt apart from the log output that is written to System.out while the application starts. If 0, the first prompt waits promptDelay.

promptDelay.label: consumer
promptDelay.description: The delay in milliseconds before each prompt of promptMessage, except the first one when initialPromptDelay is set.

promptMessage.label: consumer
promptMessage.description: The text that the consumer prints to System.out before it reads each line from System.in, for example Enter a command: (no new line is added). Only printed for kind in, and not with scanStream.

readLine.label: consumer
readLine.description: Whether the consumer reads the stream line by line and creates an exchange with a String body for each line, or for each group of groupLines lines. If false, the consumer reads the stream to its end and creates one exchange with all the bytes as byte[] body; with scanStream, each exchange holds the bytes read in one scan.

retry.label: consumer
retry.description: Whether the consumer opens the stream again at its end and after it failed to open or read it, somewhat like tail --retry. Only used with scanStream. A file is then read again from the beginning, and the request to httpUrl is sent again. Without fileWatcher this happens at each end of the stream, so enable fileWatcher to read a file again only after it changed.

scanStream.label: consumer
scanStream.description: Whether the consumer keeps reading the stream after its end, like the Unix tail -f command, and waits scanStreamDelay each time it finds no new data. The consumer opens the stream in its reading thread, so a file that does not exist yet or a URL that cannot be reached does not fail the start, and is opened again later only with retry. A scanned stream never completes, so the CamelStreamComplete header is always false.

scanStreamDelay.label: consumer
scanStreamDelay.description: The delay in milliseconds before the consumer reads again when it finds no new data in the stream. Only used with scanStream. After the stream could not be opened or read, the consumer waits at least one second.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

appendNewLine.label: producer
appendNewLine.description: Whether the producer writes the line separator of the operating system (System.lineSeparator()) after each message body.

autoCloseCount.label: producer
autoCloseCount.description: The number of messages after which the producer closes the file of kind file. The next message opens the file again for another batch of messages. If 0, the producer keeps the file open until it stops. System.out and System.err are never closed, and the stream of kind header is closed after each message.

closeOnDone.label: producer
closeOnDone.description: Whether the producer closes the file of kind file after the last message of a Splitter, which is the message with the exchange property CamelSplitComplete set to true. The next message opens the file again. Without it and autoCloseCount, the producer keeps the file open until it stops.

delay.label: producer
delay.description: The delay in milliseconds before the producer writes each message.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

readTimeout.label: advanced
readTimeout.description: Not used: the component applies no read timeout to any stream, including the connection to httpUrl.
